result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs finished on time, every month's inference demand was fully served, and there were no penalties. **Final net cost: $1,064M.**

| Item | $M |
|---|---|
| GPU purchases (net of broker refunds) | 919.5 |
| Power | 211.5 |
| Reserved cloud contracts | 215.4 |
| Interest | 36.8 |
| Resale income | −117.9 |
| Total spent | 1,265.4 |
| GPUs marked at their used value at the end | −284.6 |
| Power and contract payments still owed after month 23 | +83.6 |

**What happened:**
- **Months 0–3:** The supply signals said "tight", so I bought ahead. I ordered 10k gen-H GPUs from the vendor and tested both brokers with 2k each; both delivered. I also signed 40 MW of power and took two 3 kH, 24-month cloud reservations while the price was low (about $1.44M per kH-month).
- **Brokers:** A later cancelled a 4k order and B cancelled a 3k gen-N order. I stopped using them; each cancellation lost 20% of the order.
- **Launch timing:** The rumours said "around 12", "around 12" and "around 15". With each rumour off by at most 2, the only month consistent with all three was 14, and gen N did launch then, with no advance confirmation. I ordered 5k gen N from the vendor right away. It all shipped by month 18 and closed the gap for the last training window.
- **Power:** I signed 25 MW at month 9, so every GPU still had power after the original 16 MW contract ended at month 19.
- **Inference growth** looked closer to 3% than 7% (demand went from about 5.5 to 12 kH). There was no clear switch.
- **End:** I resold 6k gen-H and 3k gen-N GPUs I no longer needed in months 22–23, because selling then paid slightly more than the end-of-game valuation.

**What cost the most:** I built far too much capacity early. The first window got 145 kH-months against the 60 required, and the second got 269 against 140. Compute only counts in its own window, so that surplus was wasted. Most of the 8k gen-H ordered at month 5 and the 4k at month 10 was never needed before month 16. Buying less early and leaning on gen N after launch would probably have saved $100–200M. The third window closed with some margin (the run needed 320).

There's a belief-log note for every month, but my first three notes, months 0–2, are damaged. I separated them from the commands with periods instead of `;`, which caused two problems:
- In month 0, fragments of the note were run as commands and errored out, though the real orders still went through.
- In month 2, the note swallowed my intended `buy_gpus 4 H A`, so that order was never placed. I placed it a month later, and broker A cancelled it.
